Balance.description: How traffic picks a replica: `round-robin` (default), `random`, `least-conn` (the replica with the fewest requests in it), `p2c` (the less loaded of two random replicas), or `{ weighted: [..] }` with one weight per replica (at least one above 0).

BoundedConcurrency.description: The map form of `concurrency`: the same queue and overflow defaults as `pool`.

limit.description: Own hops that run at once, at least 1.

overflow_status.description: Status returned when the queue is full, 500–504 (default 503).

queue.description: Requests that may wait for a slot (default 0).

CacheFlavor.description: Cache flavors with a preset hit ratio and costs (estimates, see [`crate::presets`]).

ChaosEntry.description: One chaos entry of a scenario: where it applies plus the fields it sets.

bandwidth_cap.description:
Edge only: caps the edge's `bandwidth` (bytes per second, at least 1, at most the
edge's own; a whole number or text with a unit like `500KB/s`).

edge.description:
A link: the edge from one node to another (it must exist). Takes no node, endpoint or
replica; sets `latency_ms`, `jitter_ms`, `error_rate` with `error_kind` `reset` or `hang`,
`down` (a partition) and `bandwidth_cap`.

endpoint.description: `METHOD /path`: the front door of that endpoint.

error_kind.description: How a failure shows up: `status` (default), `reset`, `hang` or `malformed`.

error_status.description: Status of a failed visit, 500 to 504 (default 503).

jitter_ms.description: Edge only: random extra latency of up to this many milliseconds either way.

latency_ms.description:
Extra latency in milliseconds (at most 300000, which is `MAX_LATENCY_ADD`; a doc
attribute cannot compute it, so keep the two in step).

node.description:
A node name. With `endpoint`: only when visited through that endpoint; with `replica`:
one copy of the node.

replica.description:
With `node`: one replica of it (0-based), whatever the endpoint. Needs the node to have
that many `replicas`.

DbFlavor.description: Database flavors with preset op costs (estimates, see [`crate::presets`]).

Determinism.description: How chain draws are seeded (rule R1.34).

oneOf.description: Draws follow `seed:`: the same requests see the same timings and failures.

Draws follow a seed picked at startup and printed; replay a run with `controlled`
and that seed.

Distribution.description: A latency: `5ms` (fixed), `{ p50, p99 }` (lognormal fitted to both, p50 at most p99) or `{ mean }` (exponential). At most 1h.

balance.description:
How calls over this edge pick a replica of the callee; overrides the callee's own
`balance`.

bandwidth.description:
Link capacity: bytes per second (at least 1) as a whole number, or text with a unit like
`250KB` or `1MB/s` (KB = 1024 bytes). With a payload size, a transfer takes
`bytes / bandwidth` when alone on the link, and more while other transfers share its rate
fairly. Absent = no limit,
and no link hop.

calls.description:
Calls per request along this edge (call ratio), at least 1. Used once endpoint
chains land.

keepalive.description:
Calls a connection serves before it closes (keep-alive), 1 to 1000000, default 1000 (nginx's
`keepalive_requests`). One call in `keepalive` opens a new connection and pays the TCP (and
TLS) handshake and slow start; `1` is a new connection every call.

net.description: Network latency on this edge; absent means zero.

prob.description:
Share of requests that take this edge, above 0 and at most 1 (default 1). The default for
every `call:` step over this edge; a step's own `prob` wins. Not for caches (they keep
their hit ratio) or edges out of a gateway.

returns.description:
Size of the response body a call over this edge brings back, written like `sends`. Absent
= the size of the response the caller itself has to give.

sends.description:
Size of the request body a call over this edge carries: bytes as a whole number, or text
with a unit like `200KB` (KB = 1024 bytes; at most 1 GiB). A `call:` step may override it.
Absent = the size of the request that reached the caller (it is passed on).

tls.description:
TLS a new connection over this edge negotiates after TCP: `false` (default), `true` or
`1.3` (one extra round trip) or `1.2` (two). Costs nothing on a reused connection, and
nothing when the edge has no `net` (the round trip is its latency).

to.description: Name of the node it calls.

EdgeRef.description: The two ends of an edge in a chaos entry: `edge: { from: app, to: db }`.

EndpointConfig.description:
One `endpoints:` entry. Every field is optional; a spec route without an entry gets the
default chain.

chain.description: Steps the route's owner runs after its own `proc`; absent = the default chain.

collection.description:
Name of an in-memory collection this route reads or writes (`GET /x` lists, `GET /x/{id}`
gets, `POST /x` adds, `DELETE /x/{id}` removes); cannot be combined with `override`.

error_map.description:
Failure → response, looked up by failing node, then status (`504`), then class
(`5xx`, `4xx`); a value is a status or `{ status, body }`.

op.description:
Database operation for the chain (`read`, `write`, `scan`); default inferred from the
method and path (`GET /x/{id}` read, `GET /x` scan, anything else write).

override.description: A fixed response served instead of generated data (`status` default 200, `body`).

states.description:
Overrides for the UI states a pin can force, keyed `loading`, `empty`, `error` or
`slow`: a `status`, a `body` and a `delay` each.

total.description:
Records a paged list route reports in total, 0 to 10000 (default: seeded per route);
cannot be combined with `override` or `collection`.

Endpoints.description: A path to an endpoints file, or the endpoints inline.

oneOf.description: Path relative to this file, e.g. `kaanal.endpoints.yaml`.

ErrorMapping.description: The response for a failure: a status, or a status and a body.

anyOf.description: The same size for a request and a response.
Separate sizes; a missing side keeps its default.

HeaderBytes.description:
What an HTTP call carries besides its body (`header_bytes:` at the top of the file): one size
for a request and for a response, or `{ request, response }`. Default 600 B and 400 B, a labelled
estimate; `0` turns headers off.

request.description: Header bytes of a request: bytes as a whole number, or text with a unit like `1KB`.

response.description: Header bytes of a response, written like `request`.

Hold.description: What a node's slot covers (`hold:`), for a node that calls others.

oneOf.description:
The slot is held only while the node does its own work. A server that waits on its calls
without a thread (an event loop: Node, Go, async Python). The default.

The slot is held from the moment the request is admitted until everything the node calls
has answered. A server with a thread or worker per request (Tomcat, sync Gunicorn, Puma,
PHP-FPM): a slow dependency fills the node's slots and its queue grows.

JourneyConfig.description: One endpoint in a profile's mix.

req_bytes.description:
Size of each request body: bytes as a whole number, or text with a unit like `2KB` (KB =
1024 bytes; at most 1 GiB). Default 0: no link or `per_kb` cost.

resp_bytes.description:
Size of each response body, written like `req_bytes` (default: the size of one generated
body for a route with a response schema, else 0).

weight.description: Relative share of the profile's rate (above 0, default 1).

anyOf.description: The same rate sending and receiving.

NodeBandwidth.description:
A node's network card (`bandwidth:`): a rate (bytes per second as a whole number, or text
with a unit like `250KB/s`), one for both directions or `{ out, in }`. Each direction is at
least 1; a missing side of the pair is unlimited.

in.description: Rate this node can receive: bytes per second, or text like `1MB/s`.

out.description:
Rate this node can send (its calls out and its responses): bytes per second, or text
like `1MB/s`.

NodeConfig.description: One node in `nodes:`. `type` selects the kind; each kind rejects fields it does not have.

oneOf.description: A reverse proxy / API gateway / load balancer.

balance.description:
How traffic entering this node picks a replica (default `round-robin`); a calling edge
may override it.

bandwidth.description:
This node's network card, in bytes per second (at least 1): one number for both
directions or `{ out, in }`. Each copy has its own send and receive pipe; payloads share
the rate fairly, so calls to different services share the uplink. Absent = no limit.

concurrency.description:
Most requests this node serves at once, as a number (the rest wait without limit) or a
map `{ limit, queue, overflow_status }` (the rest wait up to `queue`, then get
`overflow_status`). Absent = unlimited.

flavor.description: Cosmetic label shown in status output (`nginx`, `envoy`); not a preset.

hold.description:
What a slot of this node covers (default `own`): `own` holds a slot only while the node
does its own work; `call` holds it until everything the node calls has answered, as a
thread-per-request server does, so a slow dependency fills this node's slots too.

locale.description:
Locale pack for the data this node's routes generate, e.g. `en-US`; beats the top-level
`locale`.

per_kb.description:
Extra processing time per KB of payload (request and response each, once per body), a
duration like `proc`. Absent = none.

rate_limit.description:
Token-bucket limit on how fast requests may reach this node: `rps` refilled per second,
at most `burst` at once; beyond it the request fails with 429.

replicas.description:
Copies of this node, 1 to 64 (default 1). Each has its own slots, queue, pool and rate
limit; `balance` picks one per request.

timeout.description:
Deadline for a call to this node: queue wait plus its own work plus everything it calls
downstream. When it passes, the caller gets a 504 (`timeout`) while the work already
running keeps its slot until it ends. `0 < timeout <= 5 min`; absent = no deadline.

UI-state pins applied together with the chaos: each forces one endpoint to

call.description: Node to call; an edge from the running node to it must exist.

chain.description: Inline body for a service or monolith callee.

op.description: Op for this step (database or monolith with inline ops).

prob.description: Share of requests that take this call; default is the edge's `prob`. One draw covers every `repeat`.

repeat.description: Sequential calls; default is the edge's `calls`.

via.description: One of the callee's endpoints, `"METHOD /path"`; uses that endpoint's chain and op.

with.description: A named chain of the callee (its `chains:`).

cache.description: Cache node to look up; a hit ends the enclosing sequence.

parallel.description: Branches (a step or a list of steps) that start together; the first failure fails the block.

duration.description: Simulated time of a run (default 60s); a run request may override it.

journeys.description: The mix: each journey gets `rps × weight ÷ sum of weights`.

rps.description: Total requests per second across all journeys (0.000001 to 1000000).

warmup.description: Simulated time before results count (default a tenth of the duration).

claims.description:
Extra claims in this user's token (string, number or boolean; at most 32); they win
over the node's `claims`. Same reserved names.

password.description:
Plain-text password, at most 256 bytes. Never logged or printed. Must be text: put a
number or `true` in quotes.

roles.description: Roles put into the token's `roles` claim (at most 32).

scopes.description:
OAuth scopes, joined with spaces into the token's `scope` claim (at most 32; each
printable ASCII without space, `"` or `\`).

username.description: Login name and the token's `sub`: unique per node, 1 to 256 bytes.

data.description:
Field dictionary for generated data, relative to this file. Default: `data.yaml` next
to this file, when it exists.

determinism.description:
`controlled` (default): timings and failures follow `seed`, so a run can be replayed.
`realistic`: a seed is picked at startup (and printed), so runs differ like a real system.

endpoints.description:
Per-endpoint chains, overrides and error maps: a path to a YAML file (relative to this
file, e.g. `kaanal.endpoints.yaml`) or an inline map keyed by `"METHOD /path"`.

header_bytes.description:
Header bytes an HTTP call carries on top of its body: a size for both sides, or
`{ request, response }`. Default 600 B and 400 B (estimates); `0` is off. Charged on every
wire transfer and on the per-KB cost of an HTTP node, so only a topology that has a
`bandwidth`, a `per_kb` or a storage `throughput` is affected.

locale.description:
Locale pack for generated data (names, places, phone, currency), e.g. `en-US`. A node's
own `locale` wins. Default `en-IN`. A built-in tag, or a pack you add as
`locales/<tag>.yaml` next to this file; `kaanal validate` lists the available tags.

nodes.description: Nodes by name, in file order (deterministic error messages).

port.description: Port for the HTTP server (mock + control API share it). Defaults to 8080.

scenarios.description:
Named chaos scenarios (a list of chaos entries each), switched on and off at runtime.
More can live in `scenarios/NAME.yaml` next to this file.

seed.description: Master RNG seed: same seed → same data, timings and failure patterns.

site.description: Static files served next to the mocks, a folder relative to this file.

traffic.description: Named load profiles for the simulator: a total rate and a weighted mix of endpoints.
